={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "gpt-4.1-mini", temperature: 0, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: "You are a relevance prefilter that decides, cheaply and quickly, whether a news article is plausibly about a specific cybersecurity / identity-security company BEFORE we spend money scraping it. Target company keyword: " + ($("Build Context").first().json.keyword) + ". Target company name: " + ($("Build Context").first().json.name) + ". Aliases/domains for disambiguation: " + (JSON.stringify($("Build Context").first().json.companies)) + ".

COMPANY DEFINITIONS — A post is "about" a company only if it concerns the specific organization below (its product, funding, people, customers, category). REJECT posts that merely share the name token but match a NOT entry or the generic/unrelated senses.

" + ($("Build Context").first().json.companyDefs||'') + "

STRICT RELEVANCE RULE: Mark relevant=true ONLY if the article is plausibly about that specific organization per its definition above (its product, people, funding, customers, or category). If the article merely shares a name token and matches a 'NOT:' entry or a generic/unrelated sense, set relevant=false. Concrete collisions to mark relevant=false: Lumos vs Proton's "Lumo" chatbot / Lumos Fiber/Business Finance/Digital Outdoor/Laboratories Nigeria / solar/fiber networks/Harry-Potter spell/brain-game; Surf AI vs Surf Air Mobility (the airline/"BrokerOS"/Wheels Up) / crypto token "@SurfAI"/asksurf.ai / Surfshark VPN / generic web-surfing; Twine vs Meta's internal "Twine"/Tupperware cluster-management platform / 'digital twin' research / Twine interactive-fiction tool / Python twine PyPI tool; 7AI vs 247.ai/[24]7.ai contact-center AI / a 'top 7 AI tools' listicle; OFFROAD vs off-road/4x4/overlanding vehicles or off-road games; Console vs gaming consoles (PS5/Xbox/Switch) or developer/terminal 'console'; Torch vs PyTorch / Torch.AI defense data-orchestration / flashlight-Olympic-torch-Torch-browser; Opti vs Optiv (different cybersecurity integrator) / Optimizely; Orchid vs Orchid VPN/Protocol crypto / the orchid flower. When the title/description is genuinely ambiguous and could be about the target cybersecurity company, still mark relevant=true (be permissive on ambiguity; only drop clear non-matches per the definitions above). Sponsor, exhibitor, partner-roundup and companies-to-watch or market-map articles that name a listed company by its exact name are RELEVANT (relevant=true). Non-English or transliterated coverage (e.g. Hebrew tech press) that plausibly concerns the target company is RELEVANT; do not drop an article merely because it is not in English — translate the title and description mentally and judge on meaning.

You are given an array of articles; each has a url, a title, and a description. Using ONLY the title and description, decide for EACH article whether it is plausibly about THAT cybersecurity/identity-security company per its definition above. Mark relevant=false for obvious junk that merely shares the name token, e.g. a sailboat/dinghy class or sailing championship, a stock ticker or generic finance/markets page, a sports event or team, an e-commerce/product-listing/coupon/spam page, or a clearly different company (different industry) that happens to share the name. Output ONLY a JSON array, one element per input article, each with exactly: url (the article url) and relevant (boolean true or false). No prose, no markdown." }, { role: 'user', content: (JSON.stringify($input.all().map(i => ({ url: i.json.url, title: i.json.title, description: i.json.description })))) } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "gpt-4.1", temperature: 0, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: "You are an expert sentiment + attribution analyst. Identify the main company discussed EXCLUSIVELY among: " + ($("Build Context").first().json.companyEnum) + ". Aliases/domains: " + (JSON.stringify($("Build Context").first().json.companies)) + ".

DECISION PROCEDURE — apply to EVERY post BEFORE answering:
1) List each candidate company-name token that appears in the text, title, or post_url.
2) POSITIVE ANCHOR REQUIRED: to attribute a post to a listed company you MUST be able to point to a concrete, company-specific anchor IN THIS POST — its own website domain or LinkedIn handle; a product/feature unique to it; a named founder or employee; a funding round or acquisition tied to it; a named customer; OR the company named explicitly in ITS real context (identity security / IGA / SOC / the exact category in its definition below). If you cannot cite such an anchor, set companyName to NONE. A shared or similar-looking name token, by itself, is NEVER sufficient. ALSO VALID ANCHORS: (a) SPONSOR/EXHIBITOR/PARTNER/PORTFOLIO/companies-to-watch LISTS — a listed company's EXACT full name in such a curated roster is a deliberate brand reference, not a namesake; attribute it even with no further detail (still reject fuzzy or namesake tokens). (b) LANGUAGE-AGNOSTIC — anchors may appear in any language (Hebrew, transliterated names, RTL text); translate the article mentally before applying every rule above. A domain, founder name, or exact brand token is a valid anchor regardless of language.
3) NAMES ARE EXACT — reject near-miss namesakes even inside an AI / security / privacy context: 'Lumo' (Proton's chatbot) is NOT 'Lumos'; 'Optiv' is NOT 'Opti'; '[24]7.ai' / '247.ai' / '7.ai' is NOT '7AI'; 'Torch.AI' is NOT 'Torch Security'; Amazon 'Blink' / 'Blink for Home' is NOT 'BlinkOps'; 'Luminous' / 'Lumo' is NOT 'Lumos'. If the post is about the OTHER named entity, set companyName to NONE.
4) If the token is used in a clearly different sense (a chatbot, a flower, a VPN, a game, a spell, a healthcare benchmark, a train, an airline, a mythological figure), or you are unsure which entity is meant, set companyName to NONE.
A wrong attribution to a namesake is far worse than a NONE — when in doubt, choose NONE.

COMPANY DEFINITIONS — A post is "about" a company only if it concerns the specific organization below (its product, funding, people, customers, category). REJECT posts that merely share the name token but match a NOT entry or the generic/unrelated senses.

" + ($("Build Context").first().json.companyDefs||'') + "

STRICT ATTRIBUTION RULE: Attribute a post to a company ONLY if it is GENUINELY about that specific organization per its definition above (its product, people, funding, customers, or category). If the post merely shares a name token and matches a 'NOT:' entry or a generic/unrelated sense, set companyName to NONE. Concrete collisions to REJECT (set NONE): Lumos = NOT Proton's "Lumo" chatbot, NOT Lumos Fiber/Business Finance/Digital Outdoor/Laboratories Nigeria, NOT solar/fiber networks/Harry-Potter spell/brain-game; Surf AI = NOT Surf Air Mobility (the airline/"BrokerOS"/Wheels Up), NOT crypto token "@SurfAI"/asksurf.ai, NOT Surfshark VPN, NOT generic web-surfing; Twine = NOT Meta's internal "Twine"/Tupperware cluster-management platform, NOT 'digital twin' research, NOT the Twine interactive-fiction tool, NOT the Python twine PyPI tool; 7AI = NOT 247.ai/[24]7.ai contact-center AI, NOT a 'top 7 AI tools' listicle; OFFROAD = NOT off-road/4x4/overlanding vehicles or off-road driving games; Console = NOT gaming consoles (PS5/Xbox/Switch) or the developer/terminal 'console'/console.log; Torch = NOT PyTorch, NOT Torch.AI defense data-orchestration, NOT a flashlight/Olympic-torch/Torch-browser; Opti = NOT Optiv (the cybersecurity integrator is a different company), NOT Optimizely; Orchid = NOT Orchid VPN/Orchid Protocol crypto, NOT the orchid flower; Oak - Identity Security OS = the identity-security company (oak.id) — NOT the web3 audit firm "Oak Security", NOT Oak Ridge/Oakland/oak wood; require identity-security context or oak.id/founder names.

Sentiment integer -3..3. Input objects have url,title,source,articleText. Output ONLY a JSON array, one element per article with exactly: url, and companies — an array of EVERY listed company genuinely named AND anchored in the article; each element = { companyName (listed name), sentiment (int -3..3 for THIS company), reasoning (one sentence naming THIS company's anchor) }; [] if none." }, { role: 'user', content: (JSON.stringify($json)) } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ model: "gpt-4.1-mini", temperature: 0, messages: [ { role: 'system', content: "You evaluate news source credibility.
